**Landing state as read.** A `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` account approved twice at 2026-10-27T01:52Z on this head and armed auto-merge (merge method `merge`); at 2026-10-27T02:03Z the PR was still `open`, `merged: false`, `mergeable_state: blocked` (waiting on checks). This record is owed on the head regardless and is rendered from `git show 3add67c7:PATH` against `origin/main` at `abb90460`, never from the shared checkout. The PR's recorded base `abb90460` is not an ancestor of the head: the merge-base is `756220c4`, and `main` moved from `756220c4` to `abb90460` on none of the three files this PR touches (`git diff --stat 756220c4 abb90460 -- scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs skills/objectstack-api/` is empty), so the three-file diff below is the whole PR and the dev's "read off main at 756220c4" readings hold on the live tip.

**Check-runs on `3add67c7`** (read twice, last at 2026-10-27T02:03Z, not waited for): 51 runs, 34 `success`, 16 `skipped` (UI, docs, dogfood-regression and opt-in lanes the path filter turned off), 1 `in_progress` (`TypeScript Type Check`). Every gate this PR can move is green: `Type Check · source gates` (the lane that runs `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` and its `--self-test`, `check:ratchet-remedy-authority`, `check:skill-docs` and `check:skill-refs` — read off `lint.yml` lines 5326, 5458, 5582, 5589–5590 under job `typecheck-source-gates`, not the "Lint · repo & tooling gates" lane the sibling brief assumed), `Type Check · consumer gates` (runs `check:skill-examples`, line 6463, job `typecheck-consumers`) — success at 2026-10-27T01:56Z and later, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, Build Core and Test Core 1–8. Nothing red.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Every new sentence is true of the spec and the implementation on `origin/main`.** Three hunks, 27 added lines in `SKILL.md`, each read line by line:

1. *Public-form file field* (`SKILL.md` lines 104–111, inside "Public (anonymous) Form Endpoints", which the card's `SKILL.md:75-100` names). RIGHT on every clause. `FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES` is `image, file, avatar, video, audio` (`field-value.zod.ts:306-308`). The rule id is the exported constant `PUBLIC_FORM_FILE_FIELD = 'public-form-file-field'`; its registry row is `tier: 'gating'`, `commands: ALL` where `AUTHORING_COMMANDS = ['validate', 'build', 'lint']` (`authoring-rules.ts:167, 462, 1584-1593`) — so "at `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint`" is exact. "And at the view's publish": `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME` with `runtimeTypes: ['view']`, and `runtime-gate.ts:584-592` selects rules whose `surfaces` include `runtime-publish` for the written type — the registry comment states the view's publish is refused at the key and an `object` write is deliberately not covered; the skill's sentence claims only the view's publish, which is what holds. "A visitor has no upload door to mint a `sys_file` id" is the rule's own header wording. The submit-door sentence: `form-routes.ts:650-663` pushes `{ field, code: 'invalid_value', message, label }` for every file-typed field carrying a non-empty value and throws `validationFailure(...)`, whose constructor (`packages/types/src/validation-failure.ts:76-82`) is what both dispatcher exits map to `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` + `details.fields[]`; the file's own comments at 585 and 616 call this "the flat `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `fields[]`", so "flat" is the code's term, not the dev's. The qualifier "a form published before that rule" is the only population that can still carry a file field after the rule, and the refusal fires on any such submission. The prescription "collect the file on a signed-in form instead" is ruling C's own route as the rule header records it.

2. *Import `applyOn`* (`SKILL.md` lines 269–275, directly after the derived-verbs table whose `import` row is the card's `SKILL.md:253` neighbourhood). RIGHT. `ImportMappingSchema` is the union of the `{ Column: field }` record and `z.array(FieldMappingEntrySchema)` (`export.zod.ts:241-245`); `applyOn: ColumnApplyOnSchema.default('always')` sits on the entry only (`export.zod.ts:174`; the enum is `['create', 'always']`, `column-apply-on.zod.ts`). The door: `prepareImportRequest` reads `applyOn` only in the `Array.isArray(body.mapping)` branch, treats `undefined` as `always`, and returns `{ status: 400, code: 'INVALID_REQUEST' }` for any value outside the pair (`import-prepare.ts:610-627`); both routes (`data-action-routes.ts:369`, `:483`) call it on the raw body with no prior Zod parse that could answer first, so "any other value is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`" is exactly what the door answers. The record form silently ignores `applyOn` (it keeps only string values), so "only the entry form carries `applyOn`" is right. "A re-run `upsert` refreshes the `always` columns and leaves a value an admin set since": `import-runner.ts:690-694` builds the update patch as `if (!createOnly.has(k) || keySet.includes(k)) patch[k] = v`. "A create-only column is still read for matching": true — `findExisting` reads `data[f]` for every key-set field regardless of `applyOn` — and the runner additionally still WRITES a create-only column on update when it belongs to the matched key set (the `|| keySet.includes(k)` arm). The skill's sentence is true as written; it leaves that corner unsaid, which is a scope choice, not a falsehood (an author who marks a match key create-only gets the key written back unchanged).

3. *`FLOW_FAILED` details* (`SKILL.md` lines 372–380, inside "Error Envelopes & the Code Ledger"). RIGHT. `FlowFailureDetailsSchema` is exactly `errorMessage?` ("the flow author's own failure text"), `summary?` (`FlowRunSummarySchema`, "which node failed") and `innerRefusal?` (`automation-api.zod.ts:585-602`); `FlowInnerRefusalSchema` is `{ code: ErrorCode, message: string }` with `code` "in its WIRE spelling (e.g. `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`)" (lines 334–344). The three example codes the skill lists are the ones the runtime CHANGELOG names for the node catch arms. The doors: the trigger route is `POST /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger` (`automation-api.zod.ts:43`; the skill's `{name}` spelling matches the file's own `/data/{object}/import` convention), and the dispatch table at `automation.ts:2041-2048` / `endpoint-executor.ts:476-480` answers "ran and failed" with `400 FLOW_FAILED` at the trigger, resume, `/actions` and declared-endpoint doors (the "409 at the trigger door" line in `endpoint-executor.ts:487` is the history the table replaced, not the current answer). The render order `userMessage` → `details.innerRefusal` → `message` is NOT the dev's invention: it is the CHANGELOG's own "For consumers" sentence on the entry that landed `innerRefusal` ("render a refused run the way a record form renders a refused save: the top-level `userMessage` when present, then `details.innerRefusal`, then `message`"), and `userMessage` is `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage` (`contract.zod.ts:93`). "Absent keys mean the run produced none — never invent an empty" is the schema's own "absent means absent, never an invented empty".

**(b) Cuts.** None. The diff removes nothing from the package (0 deletions in `SKILL.md` and the eval file; `references/_index.md` byte-identical, 3200 bytes). The card names no stale lines and the base package has 0 hits for `applyOn`, `innerRefusal`, `FLOW_FAILED` and `file field` (`git grep -c` on `756220c4`), so no duplicate existed to cut; ruling A's "削重复 first" is satisfied vacuously and the PR body says so.

**(c) Ratchet row.** The script's measure is `Math.ceil(Buffer.byteLength(text, 'utf8') / 4)` with one exclusion, the indented release-stamp line of a `SKILL.md` (`check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs:49, 77-113`). Recomputed by hand over the head blobs (a byte count, not a run): `endpoints-auth-routes.json` is 4936 bytes on the head → ceil(4936/4) = **1234**, and 4156 bytes on the base → 1039; the new row is `1234` — pinned AT the measurement, zero headroom, no smuggled room. The row's arithmetic checks: +780 bytes = 4936 − 4156; +192 = 1234 − 1042; the 3 absorbed tokens = 1042 − 1039. `SKILL.md` is 20532 bytes on the head; minus the 20-byte stamp line → 20512/4 = **5128**, under the untouched ceiling 6314 (base 18782 − 20 → 4691), so no second row moves and none should. The raise rule (header lines 128–130) requires "a PR whose body quotes a maintainer ruling authorizing it"; the script itself reads no PR body, so the evidence is the body and the row comment, and both quote the tap 「A:先削重复,余额按实测提高」 verbatim with the card's title, the date and the per-file before/after. The row comment follows the shape of the 2026-08-31 precedent block (ruling quoted untranslated, paid-down-first statement, arithmetic) and sits inside the `CEILINGS` map, not between the precedent block and the SHRINK-ONLY doc comment that `check-ratchet-remedy-authority` anchors on (placement warning at lines 294–301); that gate ran green in `Type Check · source gates`. No eslint `max-len` rule exists anywhere in the repo's config (0 hits), and `Lint · ESLint` is green, so the long comment lines are not a lint risk. The "0 duplicate bytes" claim, judged on the eval file itself: fixtures 1–5 are five distinct prompts (declarative endpoint, anonymous endpoint budget, webhook gap, auth providers, `apiMethods` derivation) and no sentence recurs between them; the only phrase shared with anything is "the flat `public` + `permissions` pair" in fixture 4, which the SKILL.md also carries at line 322 — a different file, and the ratchet prices per file. The claim holds.

**(d) Eval.** One fixture, id 6, ids 1–6 unique and sequential, the file's existing shape (`prompt` / `expected_output` / `files: []` / `assertions`). Every `must_contain` token (`applyOn`, `'create'`, `sourceField`, `targetField`) appears in `expected_output`; `must_not_contain: ["writeMode: 'insert'"]` is consistent with the expected `writeMode: 'upsert'` and with the import door's semantics. The expected output's mechanics match the runner (written on create, left out of the patch on a match, others default `always`). The card-specific acceptance asks one eval for the import and that is the one present; the shared Acceptance's "every new teaching gets an eval prompt" is met for the import teaching only — the `FLOW_FAILED` and public-form-file teachings carry no eval. The card's own text resolves that conflict in the dev's favour (the card-specific line "one eval for the import" is the narrower, later instruction, the dispatch order says "the card asks one eval, for the import", and the dev's report declares the scope), so this is a boundary note, not a failure. The package has no evals README or index counting prompts (three files in the tree), so nothing else needs updating.

**(e) Wanted lines met, nothing beyond.** All three Wanted items land in the named sections (verified above). Line 1 of `SKILL.md` (`version` frontmatter, PR #25640's line) is unchanged — the first five lines of base and head are identical. No file outside the claim + amendment surface: the three paths are `skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md`, `skills/objectstack-api/evals/endpoints-auth-routes.json` and the one `CEILINGS` row in `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`. Line readings claimed in the body are exact: `SKILL.md` 417 → 444, eval 55 → 65, `_index.md` 46 → 46, package 463 → 490.

**(f) PR body shape.** Line 1 is the harness attribution HTML comment, line 2 the harness's `_Requested by_` line, line 3 `Fixes #26299`, lines 4–5 `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, each line-initial and each occurring exactly once. os-dev.md on `main` (line 323) exempts the harness-written attribution comment on line 1 ("原样留、只报") and wants `Fixes` "紧随其后"; the harness wrote two lines, and `Fixes` follows that block on line 3. `clause2-line.mjs`'s reader is `CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE = /^[ \t]*...Clause-②...:(.*)$/` (line-initial, any line of the body), so the declaration lines are read wherever they sit; the template puts them under `## Verification`, os-dev.md after `Fixes`, and this body satisfies both readers with one pair. The CI checks that parse the closing keyword (`The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`) are green on the head, which is the proof the attribution comment did not hide `Fixes` from any parser. `## 维护者速读` carries the six labels in order; 需要你做的 names one action (approve / Merge when ready — right for Tier H); 先看 names three hunks with line numbers; 两分钟验证 is one command with the expected sight, and the sight it promises (`SKILL.md 5128 / 6314`, `endpoints-auth-routes.json 1234 / 1234 (+0)`) is the dev's paraphrase of the script's report lines, whose real wording the body's own details block quotes (`... is 5128 tokens (ceiling 6314; headroom 1186)` / `... is 1234 tokens (ceiling 1234; headroom 0)`) — a reader grepping the output finds the numbers, so the verification works as written. English sections What changes / Tests / Acceptance notes / Verification are present with readings folded into details blocks; the extra `## Why` and `## Human Minimum` come from `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (landed on `main` at `756220c4`, after dispatch); os-dev.md's 英文节序 line names an order and forbids no extra section, and the dev named the conflict rather than picking silently. The commit's trailer pair is model-free. The body reports no model name.

**(g) Report.** os-dev-report 6431775093 carries `issue`, `status: done`, `branch: claude/project-thread-i1b4v5` (= the claim's branch), `pr`, `session`, `premise_still_valid`, `summary`, `tests`, `gates`, `dogfood_battery: n/a` (no `!`, no narrowing arm — right), `mcp_calls: 0`, `api_writes: 3` with endpoints, `line_budget`, `deviations` (7), `open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings` (2). `files_changed` / `rules_retired` are absent, and os-dev.md's JSON template on `main` (lines 362–384) does not list them, so nothing is missing. One note: the report's `summary` and first deviation name the served models by id; the dispatch order's ban reads "no model name anywhere in the commit or PR", and both the commit message and the PR body are clean — the card comment is outside the ban's letter, so this is a process note, not a defect.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: `skills/objectstack-api/` carries no `package.json` (tree: `SKILL.md`, `evals/endpoints-auth-routes.json`, `references/_index.md`), `scripts/**` publishes no npm package, and `Check Changeset` is green on the head. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are correct — the skill teaches keys the protocol already carries (`FieldMappingEntry.applyOn`, `FlowFailureDetails`, the lint rule), no accept set moves. Both declaration lines are line-initial and the value is the first thing after the colon.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev's out-of-scope note 1** — `SeedColumn.applyOn` (same `ColumnApplyOnSchema`, `seed.zod.ts`) is objectstack-data's surface and is untaught there: confirmed, `git grep -c applyOn origin/main -- skills/objectstack-data/` is 0 hits. That belongs to the #26297 (objectstack-data) card's dev or a follow-up card on that package; it is a 收班简报 note for the seat, not this PR's debt.
- **Dev's out-of-scope note 2** — the premise read looked for the anonymous-form file refusal in `packages/spec/src/api` while it lives in `packages/lint` + `packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts`: confirmed by reading; a process note for the seat's premise-read recipe, nothing to file.
- **Eval coverage** — only the import teaching has an eval (card-specific acceptance), while the shared Acceptance's "every new teaching gets an eval" would want two more (`FLOW_FAILED` details, public-form file field). The card's own narrower line and the dispatch order settle this PR; the seat may want to carry "evals for API2/API3" as a note for a later ratchet-paying card. Not a defect of this head.
- **PR-template vs os-dev.md** — the template's declaration-lines-under-Verification layout and os-dev.md's after-`Fixes` layout are both satisfied by one pair here, and the template's `## Why` / `## Human Minimum` are extra sections os-dev.md does not forbid. The two documents should converge in os-dev.md, and the harness's two-line attribution block (comment + `_Requested by_`) should be named in os-dev.md line 323, which today reads as one line. 收班简报 note; nothing for this PR.
- **Lane naming** — the ratchet, `check:ratchet-remedy-authority`, `check:skill-docs` and `check:skill-refs` run in `Type Check · source gates`, and `check:skill-examples` in `Type Check · consumer gates`, not in the "Lint · …" lanes the reviewer briefs assumed. A note for the brief template, not for this PR.
- **Base reconciliation** — base `abb90460` vs merge-base `756220c4`: `main` moved on none of the three touched files, the ratchet row on `main` still reads `1042`, so the merge carries exactly this diff.
